courses.title: AI for All: From Basics to GenAI Practice
courses.description: Artificial Intelligence, or AI, is transforming society in many ways. From speech recognition to self-driving cars, to the immense possibilities offered by generative AI. This introductory course provides invaluable insights into the evolving landscape of AI. We begin with an introduction to AI, covering basic concepts and principles. Next, we cover Generative AI (GenAI) and the next frontiers in AI, where you will learn about AI Agents, autonomous systems capable of complex reasoning and decision-making; Physical AI, where intelligent systems interact with the physical world, such as in robotics; and AI factories, the scalable infrastructure making it all possible. We end the course by exploring graphical processing units (GPUs) and their crucial role in transitioning AI from concept to reality. The course includes a video demo where you'll see GenAI in action by looking at one of its most exciting applications, image generation.
learning_objectives: Express how AI is transforming society
Explain terminology and concepts related to AI
Describe the emergence of Generative AI applications and their content creation capabilities
Describe the concepts of AI agents, physical AI, and AI factories, and describe how these technologies work together
Detail the evolution of GPU computing and its contribution to the AI revolution
Try a GenAI application yourself
courses.target_audience: Seasoned professionals or beginners - anyone interested in staying ahead in today's rapidly evolving technological landscape. No technical background required.
courses.technical_requirements: None - browser-based learning via NVIDIA Online Academy
courses.notes: Entry-level course for complete beginners to AI. Covers AI use cases across healthcare, autonomous vehicles, financial services, and more. Interactive self-paced learning with video demonstrations.

courses.title: Generative AI Explained
courses.description: Generative AI describes technologies that are used to generate new content based on a variety of inputs. In recent time, Generative AI involves the use of neural networks to identify patterns and structures within existing data to generate new content. In this course, you will learn Generative AI concepts, applications, as well as the challenges and opportunities in this exciting field. This no coding course provides an overview of Generative AI concepts and applications, as well as the challenges and opportunities in this exciting field.
learning_objectives: Define Generative AI and explain how Generative AI works
Describe various Generative AI applications
Explain the challenges and opportunities in Generative AI
courses.target_audience: Upon completion, you will have a basic understanding of Generative AI and be able to more effectively use the various tools built on this technology
courses.technical_requirements: None - no coding required, browser-based learning
courses.notes: Entry-level course suitable for all audiences

courses.title: Getting Started With Deep Learning
courses.description: Businesses worldwide are using artificial intelligence to solve their greatest challenges. Deep learning is a powerful AI approach that uses multi-layered artificial neural networks to deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in tasks such as object detection, speech recognition, and language translation. In this course, you'll learn how deep learning works through hands-on exercises in computer vision and natural language processing. You'll train deep learning models from scratch, learning tools and tricks to achieve highly accurate results. You'll also learn to leverage freely available, state-of-the-art pre-trained models to save time and get your deep learning application up and running quickly.
learning_objectives: Learn the fundamental techniques and tools required to train a deep learning model
Gain experience with common deep learning data types and model architectures
Enhance datasets through data augmentation to improve model accuracy
Leverage transfer learning between models to achieve efficient results with less data and computation
Build confidence to take on your own project with a modern deep learning framework
courses.target_audience: Beginners wanting to get started with deep learning through self-paced study. Students looking to build foundation for advanced deep learning courses.
courses.technical_requirements: Understanding of fundamental programming concepts in Python 3 (functions, loops, dictionaries, arrays). Familiarity with Pandas data structures. Understanding of how to compute a regression line. Optional: Building a Brain in 10 Minutes recommended.
courses.notes: Entry-level self-paced deep learning course. Covers MNIST dataset, American Sign Language classification, CNNs, pre-trained models, and NLP with BERT. Hands-on projects include image classification, automated doggy door, and question answering. Self-paced version of similar content to instructor-led Fundamentals of Deep Learning workshop.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Deep Learning
courses.description: Businesses worldwide are using artificial intelligence to solve their greatest challenges. Healthcare professionals use AI to enable more accurate, faster diagnoses in patients. Retail businesses use it to offer personalized customer shopping experiences. Automakers use it to make personal vehicles, shared mobility, and delivery services safer and more efficient. Deep learning is a powerful AI approach that uses multi-layered artificial neural networks to deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in tasks such as object detection, speech recognition, and language translation. Using deep learning, computers can learn and recognize patterns from data that are considered too complex or subtle for expert-written software. This hands-on workshop covers the fundamental techniques and tools required to train deep learning models using PyTorch.
learning_objectives: Learn the fundamental techniques and tools required to train a deep learning model
Gain experience with common deep learning data types and model architectures
Enhance datasets through data augmentation to improve model accuracy
Leverage transfer learning between models to achieve efficient results with less data and computation
Build confidence to take on your own project with a modern deep learning framework
courses.target_audience: Developers and data scientists who want to learn deep learning fundamentals through hands-on instructor-led training
courses.technical_requirements: Understanding of fundamental programming concepts in Python 3 (functions, loops, dictionaries, arrays), familiarity with Pandas data structures, and understanding of how to compute a regression line. Desktop or laptop capable of running latest Chrome or Firefox. GPU-accelerated server access provided.
courses.notes: Instructor-led version with live support

courses.title: Introduction to Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Large Language Models (LLMs), or Transformers, have revolutionized the field of natural language processing (NLP). Driven by recent advancements, applications of NLP and generative AI have exploded in the past decade. With the proliferation of applications like chatbots and intelligent virtual assistants, organizations are infusing their businesses with more interactive human-machine experiences. Understanding how Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) can be used to manipulate, analyze, and generate text-based data is essential. Modern pre-trained LLMs can encapsulate the nuance, context, and sophistication of language, just as humans do. When fine-tuned and deployed correctly, developers can use these LLMs to build powerful NLP applications that provide natural and seamless human-computer interactions within chatbots, AI voice agents, and more. In this course, you'll learn how Transformers are used as the building blocks of modern large language models (LLMs). You'll then use these models for various NLP tasks, including text classification, named-entity recognition (NER), author attribution, and question answering.
learning_objectives: Describe how Transformers are used as the basic building blocks of modern LLMs for NLP applications
Understand how Transformer-based LLMs can be used to manipulate, analyze, and generate text-based data
Leverage pre-trained, modern LLMs to solve various NLP tasks such as token classification, text classification, summarization, and question answering
courses.target_audience: Upon completion, you will have a basic understanding of how to use transformer based models for various NLP tasks, including text classification, named-entity recognition (NER), author attribution, and question answering
courses.technical_requirements: Basic understanding of deep learning concepts and basic understanding of language modeling and Transformers
courses.notes: Foundation for all transformer-based applications

courses.title: Building Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing Applications
courses.description: Learn how to apply and fine-tune a Transformer-based Deep Learning model to Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. In this course, you'll construct a Transformer neural network in PyTorch, build a named-entity recognition (NER) application with BERT, and deploy the NER application with ONNX and TensorRT to a Triton inference server. Upon completion, you'll be proficient in task-agnostic applications of Transformer-based models.
learning_objectives: Understand how transformers are used as the basic building blocks of modern LLMs for NLP applications
Learn how self-supervision improves upon the transformer architecture in BERT, Megatron, and other LLM variants for superior NLP results
Leverage pretrained, modern LLM models to solve multiple NLP tasks such as text classification, named-entity recognition (NER), and question answering
Manage inference challenges and deploy refined models for live applications
courses.target_audience: Developers with experience in Python, understanding of deep learning frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Keras), and basic understanding of neural networks
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with Python coding and use of library functions and parameters. Fundamental understanding of a deep learning framework such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Keras. Basic understanding of neural networks. Desktop or laptop computer capable of running the latest version of Chrome or Firefox. Each participant will be provided with dedicated access to a fully configured, GPU-accelerated server in the cloud.
courses.notes: Advanced workshop for production NLP applications. Assessment includes skills-based coding assessments and multiple-choice questions. Course available in English and Simplified Chinese.

courses.title: Building Conversational AI Applications
courses.description: In this workshop, you'll learn how to quickly build and deploy a conversational AI pipeline including transcription, NLP, and speech. You'll explore automatic speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS) models and their customization in detail with the NVIDIA NeMo framework and learn how to deploy the models with Riva. Finally, you'll explore the production-level deployment performance and scaling considerations of Riva services with Helm charts and Kubernetes clusters.
learning_objectives: How to customize and deploy ASR and TTS models on Riva
How to build and deploy an end-to-end conversational AI pipeline, including ASR, NLP, and TTS models, on Riva
How to deploy a production-level conversational AI application with a Helm chart for scaling in Kubernetes clusters
courses.target_audience: Developers with basic Python programming experience, fundamental understanding of a deep learning framework (TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Keras), and basic understanding of neural networks
courses.technical_requirements: Basic Python programming experience, fundamental understanding of a deep learning framework such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Keras, and basic understanding of neural networks. Desktop or laptop computer capable of running the latest version of Chrome or Firefox. Each participant will be provided with dedicated access to a fully configured, GPU-accelerated workstation in the cloud.
courses.notes: Workshop covers introduction to conversational AI, customized conversational AI pipelines, and inference and deployment challenges. Topics include ASR model pipeline from audio to spectrogram to text, decoders, customizations, ITN, punctuation/capitalization, language ID, TTS pipeline with spectrogram generator and vocoder, text normalization, G2P conversion, and production deployment with Helm charts and Kubernetes. Assessment includes skills-based coding assessments and multiple-choice questions. Available in English.

courses.title: Building LLM Applications Using Prompt Engineering
courses.description: With enterprises racing to incorporate LLMs into everything from chatbots to large-scale document analysis, this self-paced workshop teaches the modern prompt-engineering practices needed to build real applications fast. You will work with an NVIDIA language-model NIM powered by Llama 3.1 and orchestrate prompts through LangChain to solve generative, analytical, and conversational tasks while preparing for advanced techniques such as RAG and PEFT.
learning_objectives: Apply iterative prompt engineering best practices to create LLM-based applications across diverse language tasks
Use LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) runnables, chains, and parallel composition to organize LLM workflows
Develop application code that leverages LLMs for generative writing, document analysis, chatbot experiences, structured output, and tool-using agents
courses.target_audience: Developers working with LLMs and generative AI
courses.technical_requirements: Basic Python, familiarity with APIs
courses.notes: Each learner gets access to a GPU-accelerated cloud workstation running NVIDIA LLM NIM, LangChain, and Llama 3.1 while completing skills-based coding assessments.

courses.title: Building LLM Applications Using Prompt Engineering
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop where learners build LLM applications using iterative prompt engineering, LangChain, and an NVIDIA LLM NIM powered by Llama 3.1. Topics span prompt templates, LangChain Expression Language chains, structured output, chat orchestration, and agent/tool integrations so teams can deliver production-quality workflows fast.
learning_objectives: Apply iterative prompt engineering best practices to diverse language tasks
Use LangChain (including LCEL runnables and chains) to organize LLM workflows
Build applications for generative writing, document analysis, chatbots, structured output, and tool-using agents
courses.target_audience: Developers wanting structured prompt engineering training
courses.technical_requirements: Intermediate Python skills and familiarity with LLM fundamentals; workshop provides GPU-accelerated environment
courses.notes: Agenda covers OpenAI-style prompts, streaming/batching, LCEL chains, chat messaging, structured output with Pydantic/JsonOutputParser, tool-enabled agents, and a final coding assessment using NVIDIA LLM NIM.

courses.title: Rapid Application Development Using Large Language Models
courses.description: Recent advancements in both the techniques and accessibility of large language models (LLMs) have opened up unprecedented opportunities to help businesses streamline their operations, decrease expenses, and increase productivity at scale. Additionally, enterprises can use LLM-powered apps to provide innovative and improved services to clients or strengthen customer relationships. For example, enterprises could provide customer support via AI companions or use sentiment analysis apps to extract valuable customer insights. In this course you will gain a strong understanding and practical knowledge of LLM application development by exploring the open-sourced ecosystem including pretrained LLMs, enabling you to get started quickly in developing LLM-based applications.
learning_objectives: Find, pull in, and experiment with the HuggingFace model repository and Transformers API
Use encoder models for tasks like semantic analysis, embedding, question-answering, and zero-shot classification
Work with conditioned decoder-style models to take in and generate interesting data formats, styles, and modalities
Kickstart and guide generative AI solutions for safe, effective, and scalable natural data tasks
Explore the use of LangChain for orchestrating data pipelines and environment-enabled agents
courses.target_audience: Developers with introductory deep learning (comfort with PyTorch and transfer learning preferred), and intermediate Python experience including object-oriented programming and libraries. Content covered by Getting Started with Deep Learning or Fundamentals of Deep Learning, or similar experience is sufficient.
courses.technical_requirements: Introductory deep learning, with comfort with PyTorch and transfer learning preferred. Content covered by DLI's Getting Started with Deep Learning or Fundamentals of Deep Learning courses, or similar experience is sufficient. Intermediate Python experience, including object-oriented programming and libraries. Content covered by Python Tutorial (w3schools.com) or similar experience is sufficient.
courses.notes: Course covers LLMs from fundamentals of transformers through model/agentic orchestration. Topics include: Introduction to HuggingFace and Transformers, transformer-style architecture, input-output processing with tokenizers/embeddings/attention, task-specific pipelines with encoder models, Seq2Seq with GPT-style decoders, multimodal architectures (text/images/audio), scaling text generation, and orchestration with LangChain for agentic workflows. Final assessment involves building an LLM-based application integrating text generation, multimodal learning, and orchestration. Available in English.

courses.title: Rapid Application Development Using Large Language Models
courses.description: Recent advancements in both the techniques and accessibility of large language models (LLMs) have opened up unprecedented opportunities to help businesses streamline their operations, decrease expenses, and increase productivity at scale. Additionally, enterprises can use LLM-powered apps to provide innovative and improved services to clients or strengthen customer relationships. For example, enterprises could provide customer support via AI companions or use sentiment analysis apps to extract valuable customer insights. In this course you will gain a strong understanding and practical knowledge of LLM application development by exploring the open-sourced ecosystem including pretrained LLMs, enabling you to get started quickly in developing LLM-based applications.
learning_objectives: Find, pull in, and experiment with the HuggingFace model repository and the associated Transformers API
Use encoder models for tasks like semantic analysis, embedding, question-answering, and zero-shot classification
Use decoder models to generate sequences like code, unbounded answers, and conversations
Use state management and composition techniques to guide LLMs for safe, effective, and accurate conversation
courses.target_audience: Developers and teams needing to build LLM-powered applications for business operations, customer support, and service improvement
courses.technical_requirements: Introductory deep learning, with comfort with PyTorch and transfer learning preferred. Content covered by DLI's Getting Started with Deep Learning or Fundamentals of Deep Learning courses, or similar experience is sufficient. Intermediate Python experience, including object-oriented programming and libraries. Content covered by Python Tutorial or similar experience is sufficient.
courses.notes: NOTE: This version (V1) is deprecated as of 10/15/2024. Please refer to V2! Workshop covers large language models from beginning to end, starting with fundamentals of transformers, progression into foundational large language models, and finishing in model/agent orchestration. Course outline includes: Introduction to HuggingFace, Deep Learning Intuitions of LLMs, Wrapping Models Into Task-Specific Pipelines, Encoder-Decoders for Autoregressive Seq2Seq, Cross-Attention for Multi-Modal Reasoning, Scaling to Large Foundational Decoder Models, Introduction to Stateful Agentic Systems, and Final Assessment: Building An Agent.

courses.title: Building AI Agents Using Multimodal Foundation Models
courses.description: Hands-on workshop where learners build multimodal agents capable of reasoning over video, documents, and sensor data alongside language. Starting with robotics-inspired fusion techniques, the course covers converting diverse inputs into neural-ready tensors, implementing early/late/intermediate fusion, projecting new modalities into LLMs, and orchestrating Cosmos Nemotron + NVIDIA AI Blueprints to answer natural-language questions about rich media.
learning_objectives: Convert varied data types (camera, LiDAR, PDFs) into representations suitable for neural networks
Explain and implement early, late, and intermediate fusion strategies for multimodal systems
Extract text from PDFs with OCR pipelines to feed multimodal models
Differentiate modality fusion from agent orchestration and know when to use each
Customize NVIDIA AI Blueprints with Video Search and Summarization (VSS) to answer questions about video content
courses.target_audience: Developers and architects building multimodal agents for robotics, industrial inspection, or enterprise applications that demand perception plus language reasoning
courses.technical_requirements: Basic deep learning knowledge and familiarity with frameworks such as PyTorch; comfort with Python and foundational understanding of sensor/3D data workflows
courses.notes: Course outline covers early/late fusion, intermediate fusion theory plus contrastive pretraining, cross-modal projection to turn LLMs into VLMs, Cosmos Nemotron video analysis with VSS, and an assessment converting a pretrained model to ingest a new modality.

courses.title: Augment Your LLM Using Retrieval Augmented Generation
courses.description: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) - Introduced by Facebook AI Research in 2020, is an architecture used to optimize the output of an LLM with dynamic, domain specific data without the need of retraining the model. RAG is an end-to-end architecture that combines an information retrieval component with a response generator. In this introduction we provide a starting point using components we at NVIDIA have used internally. This workflow will jumpstart you on your LLM and RAG journey.
learning_objectives: Understand the basics of Retrieval Augmented Generation
Learn about the RAG retrieval process
Learn about NVIDIA AI Foundations and the components that constitute a RAG model
courses.target_audience: Developers new to RAG wanting to enhance LLM capabilities and get started on their LLM and RAG journey
courses.technical_requirements: Basic understanding of LLMs
courses.notes: Quick 1-hour introduction to RAG concepts. Course outline includes: RAG explained, RAG ingestion and retrieval processes, NVIDIA's Canonical RAG model on NV AI Foundations, and summary. Extensive related training resources including Building RAG Agents, Prompt Engineering with LLaMA-2, technical blogs on RAFT and vector search, and GitHub examples. Provides starting point using NVIDIA internal components.

courses.title: Building RAG Agents with LLMs
courses.description: Self-paced lab on composing retrieval-augmented agents that combine dialog management, internal reasoning, and tool integrations. Learners design LangChain + LangServe pipelines, manage conversation state, embed and guardrail documents, and modularize vector store workflows so agents can answer questions about research papers without fine-tuning.
learning_objectives: Compose LLM systems that mix internal reasoning with external tools to respond predictably
Design dialog/state management plus document reasoning flows that coerce information into structured outputs
Use embedding models for similarity queries and dialog guardrails
Implement, modularize, and evaluate a RAG agent that answers questions about its corpus with no fine-tuning
courses.target_audience: Developers building RAG-based applications
courses.technical_requirements: RAG basics, vector databases, Python
courses.notes: Topics span inference interfaces, LangChain pipeline design, dialog state handling, document ingestion, semantic similarity with embeddings, guardrails, vector stores, and end-to-end evaluation/certification.

courses.title: Building RAG Agents with LLMs
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop that shows how to design, orchestrate, and deploy production-ready RAG agents. Learners work through inference interfaces, LangChain/Gradio/LangServe pipelines, dialog state management, document handling, embeddings for guardrails, and vector-store retrieval before evaluating the agent end-to-end.
learning_objectives: Compose LLM systems that mix internal reasoning with external tool use so agents respond predictably
Design dialog management and document reasoning pipelines that maintain state and produce structured outputs
Leverage embedding models for semantic similarity queries and guardrailing
Implement, modularize, and evaluate a RAG agent that answers questions about its corpus without fine-tuning
courses.target_audience: Teams implementing enterprise RAG solutions
courses.technical_requirements: RAG fundamentals, Python, cloud deployment
courses.notes: Agenda includes microservice setup, pipeline design with LangChain/Gradio/LangServe, document prep, embeddings + guardrails, vector store integration, and a final assessment demonstrating the agent.

courses.title: Evaluation and Benchmarking of RAG and Semantic Search Systems
courses.description: As large language models (LLMs) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems become integral to enterprise AI applications, the need for rigorous, domain-aware evaluation grows rapidly. This course provides a comprehensive, hands-on introduction to evaluating RAG and semantic search systems, with a strong focus on real-world enterprise requirements such as regulatory compliance, data complexity, and evolving information needs. You will explore the evolution from classic keyword-based search and BM25 ranking to modern vector stores and semantic retrieval, gaining practical experience with the latest tools and frameworks. The course covers both foundational concepts and advanced evaluation strategies, including domain-specific metrics, temporal data handling, and independent assessment of retrieval and generation components.
learning_objectives: Understand the importance and unique challenges of deploying RAG and semantic search solutions in enterprise settings, including the integration of legacy and modern retrieval systems
Gain practical experience with evaluation frameworks such as Ragas, and learn to apply techniques like LLM-as-a-Judge for both metric-based and qualitative assessment of system performance

Develop skills to generate, customize, and validate synthetic test sets that reflect realistic user queries and domain-specific requirements, supporting robust, continuous evaluation and test-driven development
Learn to independently evaluate and debug the retrieval and generation stages of RAG pipelines, using both standard and custom metrics to pinpoint and address performance bottlenecks
Explore methods for handling temporal data, domain-specific language, and evolving regulatory standards, ensuring your evaluation approach remains relevant as enterprise needs change
Apply prompt engineering and data curation techniques to steer synthetic data generation, improving the quality and relevance of your test data for both model evaluation and training
courses.target_audience: Engineers optimizing RAG system performance in enterprise settings with regulatory compliance and data complexity requirements
courses.technical_requirements: Basic familiarity with Python. Basic knowledge of LLMs and RAG concepts. Some experience with data processing and evaluation workflows is helpful but not required.
courses.notes: Critical for RAG system optimization. Comprehensive hands-on course covering evolution from keyword-based search to modern semantic retrieval. Includes synthetic data generation, independent evaluation of retrieval and generation components, handling temporal data, regulatory compliance considerations, and continuous improvement workflows. Focuses on enterprise requirements including legacy system integration.

courses.title: Techniques for Improving Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Effectiveness
courses.description: Self-paced lab on turning naive vector-database + LLM prototypes into production-grade search-and-summarize applications. Learn hybrid retrieval, orchestrated microservices, chunking strategies, and evaluation approaches that measure each design change with human/LLM-as-a-judge feedback.
learning_objectives: Build a real-world, production-grade search and summarize RAG application
Create and deploy orchestrated microservices that manage different RAG responsibilities
Employ diverse chunking techniques to prepare data for retrieval
Evaluate performance using human-as-a-judge and LLM-as-a-judge frameworks
courses.target_audience: Engineers optimizing production RAG systems
courses.technical_requirements: Strong RAG background, production experience
courses.notes: Topics span dataset prep, vector/document DB indexing, intent triage, hybrid retrieval, human/LLM judging, and full-stack web deployment using NIMs, LangChain, Redis, NextJS, FastAPI, and Docker Compose.

courses.title: Generative AI with Diffusion Models
courses.description: Self-paced deep dive into denoising diffusion models for text-to-image generation. Learners build U-Nets from scratch, implement the forward and reverse diffusion processes, add classifier-free guidance, and integrate CLIP encoders so English prompts can steer the final images. Optimization topics like group norm, GELU, and sinusoidal embeddings ensure models are production ready.
learning_objectives: Build a U-Net capable of generating images directly from noise
Train forward and reverse denoising diffusion processes to improve output quality
Control generation with context embeddings and classifier-free guidance
Use CLIP encodings to transform English text prompts into image outputs
courses.target_audience: Developers working with generative models and synthetic data
courses.technical_requirements: Deep learning experience, Python, GPU access helpful
courses.notes: Topics include U-Net construction, timestep conditioning, noise schedules, group norm, GELU, rearrange pooling, sinusoidal embeddings, categorical embeddings, Bernoulli masking, classifier-free guidance, and CLIP-driven text-to-image workflows.

courses.title: Generative AI with Diffusion Models
courses.description: Instructor-led deep dive into denoising diffusion models for text-to-image generation. Participants build and refine U-Nets, implement forward/reverse diffusion processes, add classifier-free guidance, and integrate CLIP encoders so natural-language prompts control the output. Optimization labs cover group norm, GELU, rearrange pooling, and sinusoidal embeddings before culminating in a guided text-to-image project.
learning_objectives: Build U-Net architectures that generate images starting from noise
Implement denoising diffusion processes to progressively improve image fidelity
Control image outputs using context embeddings and classifier-free diffusion guidance
Combine CLIP encodings with diffusion pipelines to translate English prompts into images
courses.target_audience: Teams implementing generative AI solutions
courses.technical_requirements: Basic understanding of deep learning concepts and familiarity with frameworks such as PyTorch (used throughout the workshop)
courses.notes: Curriculum mirrors the self-paced track: U-Nets, diffusion theory, optimization tricks (group norm, GELU, rearrange pooling, sinusoidal embeddings), classifier-free guidance with categorical embeddings and Bernoulli masks, and CLIP-driven text-to-image labs. Includes instructor coaching plus GPUs.

courses.title: Getting Started with NVIDIA Tools for Generative AI in Digital Biology
courses.description: This workshop explores the cutting-edge capabilities of NVIDIA's suite of AI tools—NVIDIA Inference Microservices (NIMs) and NVIDIA AI Blueprints—in transforming digital health solutions. Participants will gain hands-on experience in developing sophisticated AI-driven applications that can converse with healthcare data, assist researchers in clinical trials, and enhance clinician-patient interactions. The session will explore NVIDIA-optimized large language models (LLMs) as well as advanced techniques using reasoning and agentic LLM systems. Emphasis will be placed on the practical aspects of deploying these GPU-accelerated technologies and customizing them to specific digital health scenarios.
learning_objectives: Gain proficiency in utilizing Generative AI NIMs and NVIDIA AI Blueprints to construct robust AI systems for digital health applications
Acquire practical skills in utilizing NIMs within real-world digital health workflows such as clinical trials
Learn strategies for adapting and evaluating AI workflows to meet the unique demands of different digital health use cases
courses.target_audience: Developers in healthcare and life sciences
courses.technical_requirements: Basic Python understanding and basic ML understanding
courses.notes: Domain-specific generative AI for digital health. Hands-on workshop exploring NIMs and AI Blueprints for healthcare applications including clinical trials and clinician-patient interactions. Covers NVIDIA-optimized LLMs and agentic systems.

courses.title: Streamlining Drug Discovery Workflows with NVIDIA BioNeMo
courses.description: Accelerate drug discovery using AI-powered molecular generation.
learning_objectives: Use BioNeMo for drug discovery
Generate molecular structures
Optimize drug candidates with AI
courses.target_audience: Computational biologists and pharmaceutical researchers
courses.technical_requirements: Biology/chemistry background helpful, Python, AI basics
courses.notes: Highly specialized pharmaceutical application

courses.title: An Introduction to NVIDIA Cosmos for Physical AI
courses.description: Introductory, hands-on Cosmos course that shows how NVIDIA Omniverse and Cosmos work together to produce photorealistic, physics-based data that accelerates physical AI development. Learners explore text-to-world and video-to-world World Foundation Models, review accelerated data processing pipelines, and implement guardrails that ensure the generated worlds are safe and useful for downstream robotics and simulation teams.
learning_objectives: Explain how NVIDIA Omniverse and Cosmos combine to generate physics-accurate synthetic data for physical AI
Differentiate Cosmos model types such as text-to-world and video-to-world generators and understand their use cases
Review the end-to-end pipeline including video preprocessing, data curation, fine-tuning, and guardrail enforcement for Cosmos workflows
courses.target_audience: Developers and simulation engineers who need to create synthetic worlds and datasets for robotics or physical AI projects
courses.technical_requirements: Understanding of AI model training, fine-tuning, and deep learning frameworks; experience with Python programming; basic familiarity with 3D software and workflows
courses.notes: Originally presented at GTC 2025; includes link to the recorded session and highlights Cosmos data processing, guardrails, and accelerated curation workflows.

courses.title: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation
courses.description: Synthetic data generation (SDG) is a data augmentation technique necessary for increasing the robustness of models by supplying training data. With advancements in pre-trained Transformers, data scientists across all industries are learning to use them to generate synthetic training data for downstream predictive tasks. In this course, you'll explore the use of Transformers for synthetic tabular data generation. We will use credit card transactions data and the Megatron framework for the course, but this technique is broadly applicable to tabular data in general.
learning_objectives: Learn how synthetic data can improve model performance
Learn to use Transformers for Synthetic Data Generation
Go through the end-to-end development workflow for generating synthetic data using Transformers, including data preprocessing, model pre-training, fine-tuning, inference, and evaluation
courses.target_audience: Data scientists with competency in Python 3, basic understanding of Machine Learning and Deep Learning concepts, experience building ML models with tabular data, and basic understanding of language modeling and Transformers
courses.technical_requirements: Competency in the Python 3 programming language, basic understanding of Machine Learning and Deep Learning concepts and pipelines, experience building Machine Learning models with Tabular data, basic understanding of language modeling and Transformers. Related Training: Getting Started with Deep Learning.
courses.notes: Self-paced course using credit card transactions data as example, broadly applicable to all tabular data. Covers end-to-end workflow from data preprocessing through evaluation. Upon completion, participants will understand how to use transformer-based models to generate synthetic tabular data for downstream predictive tasks. Available in English.

courses.title: Applications of AI for Anomaly Detection
courses.description: Whether your organization needs to monitor cybersecurity threats, fraudulent financial transactions, product defects, or equipment health, artificial intelligence can help catch data abnormalities before they impact your business. AI models can be trained and deployed to automatically analyze datasets, define normal behavior, and identify breaches in patterns quickly and effectively. These models can then be used to predict future anomalies. With massive amounts of data available across industries and subtle distinctions between normal and abnormal patterns, it's critical that organizations use AI to quickly detect anomalies that pose a threat.
learning_objectives: Prepare data and build, train, and evaluate models using XGBoost, autoencoders, and GANs
Detect anomalies in datasets with both labeled and unlabeled data
Classify anomalies into multiple categories regardless of whether the original data was labeled
courses.target_audience: Engineers and data scientists working on cybersecurity threats, fraud detection, product quality control, and equipment health monitoring
courses.technical_requirements: Professional data science experience using Python. Experience training deep neural networks. Suggested materials to satisfy prerequisites: Getting Started with Deep Learning, Intro to Machine Learning. Desktop or laptop capable of running latest Chrome or Firefox. GPU-accelerated server access provided.
courses.notes: Practical AI application for monitoring and detection. Covers supervised learning with XGBoost, unsupervised learning with autoencoders, and GAN-based anomaly detection. Includes hands-on project using network data. Assessment-based certification. Available in English.

courses.title: Applications of AI for Predictive Maintenance
courses.description: In this workshop, you'll learn how to identify anomalies and failures in time series data, estimate the remaining useful life of the corresponding parts, and use this information to map anomalies to failure conditions. You'll be able to leverage predictive maintenance to manage failures and avoid costly unplanned downtimes. To begin, you'll learn the key challenges around identifying anomalies that can lead to costly breakdowns. We'll discuss how you can leverage your company's time-series data to predict outcomes using machine learning classification models with XGBoost. Then, you'll learn how to apply predictive maintenance procedures by using an LSTM-based model to predict the failure of a device and avoid downtime. Finally, you will experiment with autoencoders to detect anomalies by using the time series sequences from the previous steps.
learning_objectives: Use AI-based predictive maintenance to prevent failures and unplanned downtimes
Identify key challenges around detecting anomalies that can lead to costly breakdowns
Use time-series data to predict outcomes with XGBoost-based machine learning classification models
Use an LSTM-based model to predict equipment failure
Use anomaly detection with time-series autoencoders to predict failures when limited failure-example data is available
courses.target_audience: Engineers and data scientists working in manufacturing, industrial IoT, and operations. Requires experience with Python and basic understanding of data processing and deep learning.
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with Python, basic understanding of data processing and deep learning. Suggested materials to satisfy prerequisites: Python Tutorial, Getting Started with Deep Learning. Desktop or laptop computer capable of running the latest version of Chrome or Firefox. Each participant will be provided with dedicated access to a fully configured, GPU-accelerated server in the cloud.
courses.notes: Workshop covers training XGBoost models with RAPIDS for time series, training LSTM models using Keras and TensorFlow for time series, and training autoencoders for anomaly detection. Topics include preparing real data for GPU ingestion with RAPIDS cuDF, building classification models with GPU-accelerated XGBoost, preparing sequenced data for time-series model training, building LSTM models with Keras, and experimenting with LSTM and 1D convolutional autoencoders. Certificate awarded upon successful completion of assessment. Available in English.

courses.title: Introduction to Multi-Modal Data Curation and Pre-Processing for LLMs
courses.description: Generative AI models derive their understanding of language and the world from the extensive data on which they are trained. Therefore data quality is paramount to ensure that models learn accurately and generalize well, leading to more reliable outputs. NeMo Curator is a GPU-accelerated data-curation tool that improves generative AI model accuracy by processing text, image, and video data at scale for training and customization. It also provides pre-built pipelines for generating synthetic data to customize and evaluate generative AI systems.
learning_objectives: Gain an understanding of why we want to curate data
Learn the basics of a typical data curation pipelines for text, images and video
Learn about NVIDIA Cosmos and video data processing pipelines
Gain a basic understand of NeMo Curator's pre-built synthetic data generation pipelines
Learn about deduplication and personal identifiable information (PII) redaction
courses.target_audience: ML engineers and data scientists preparing datasets for model training and customization
courses.technical_requirements: Understanding of fundamental programming concepts in Python 3 such as functions, loops, dictionaries and arrays and Python 3 related libraries
courses.notes: Foundation for model customization. Course comprises eight modules covering introduction, why data curation is needed, NeMo Curator overview, text curation (Tiny Stories dataset walkthrough), image curation, video curation, synthetic data generation, and NeMo Curator resources.

courses.title: Adding New Knowledge to LLMs
courses.description: Comprehensive workshop that guides teams from raw data to a customized, deployment-ready LLM. Participants curate and clean corpora with NVIDIA NeMo Curator, generate synthetic QA data, run rigorous evaluations with benchmarks, LLM-as-a-judge, and NeMo Evaluator, and then apply CPT, SFT, and DPO to inject new knowledge and behaviors. The course closes with model optimization using TensorRT-LLM, quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation so customized models remain fast and efficient in production.
learning_objectives: Curate large-scale, high-quality datasets and generate synthetic QA data with NVIDIA NeMo Curator
Evaluate LLMs using benchmarks such as MMLU, LLM-as-a-judge workflows, and the NeMo Evaluator service
Inject new domain knowledge with Continued Pretraining (CPT)
Teach LLMs new skills for targeted tasks via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
Align tone, style, and safety requirements using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
Compress and accelerate customized models through quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation on TensorRT-LLM and NeMo
Run end-to-end customization playbooks that align LLMs to real-world enterprise applications
courses.target_audience: LLM engineers and AI teams that must inject proprietary, fast-evolving knowledge into enterprise models
courses.technical_requirements: Familiarity with Python and Jupyter notebooks, understanding of LLM concepts, and conceptual knowledge of deep learning and neural networks
courses.notes: Workshop timeline covers data curation and synthetic QA generation, multi-method LLM evaluation (benchmarks, LLM-as-a-judge, NeMo Evaluator, MLflow tracking), customization with CPT/SFT/DPO, deployment optimization with TensorRT-LLM (quantization, pruning, distillation), and a hands-on assessment aligning a Llama 3.1 8B model using NeMo-RL.

courses.title: Data Parallelism: How to Train Deep Learning Models on Multiple GPUs
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop on scaling deep learning workloads across multiple GPUs with PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel (DDP). Participants revisit SGD and batch-size effects, convert single-GPU code to DDP, and apply algorithmic techniques that preserve accuracy while maximizing throughput on multi-GPU systems.
learning_objectives: Explain how data parallel training distributes work across multiple GPUs
Refactor single-GPU training scripts to PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel
Maximize throughput by tuning batch sizes, synchronization, and communication
Maintain accuracy when scaling training to multi-GPU clusters
courses.target_audience: ML engineers scaling training to multiple GPUs
courses.technical_requirements: Experience training deep learning models in Python and familiarity with PyTorch plus distributed computing concepts
courses.notes: Agenda covers SGD/batch-size theory, PyTorch DDP implementation patterns, accuracy considerations, and a skills-based assessment using cloud-hosted GPU workstations.

courses.title: Model Parallelism: Implement Billion Parameter Language Models
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop focused on training and deploying billion-parameter models across multi-node clusters. Participants train GPT-style networks with data parallelism, then layer on activation checkpointing, gradient accumulation, tensor/pipeline parallelism, and optimization techniques using PyTorch, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, and Slurm before deploying to production with TensorRT-LLM and Triton.
learning_objectives: Train neural networks across multiple servers with PyTorch, Megatron-LM, and DeepSpeed
Use activation checkpointing, gradient accumulation, and mixed parallelism to manage memory footprint
Profile training performance to tune architecture and throughput
Deploy very large multi-GPU models using TensorRT-LLM and NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
courses.target_audience: Engineers working with very large models
courses.technical_requirements: Strong PyTorch background plus experience with deep learning and data parallel training concepts
courses.notes: Agenda spans large-model training fundamentals, tensor/pipeline parallelism, Mixture-of-Experts, TensorRT-LLM/Triton deployment, and an assessment deploying a GPT checkpoint.

courses.title: Model Parallelism: Building and Deploying Large Neural Networks
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop for training and deploying massive neural networks using activation checkpointing, gradient accumulation, tensor/pipeline parallelism, and Triton deployment techniques. Attendees train GPT-scale models across multi-server clusters, profile performance, then package the resulting checkpoints with TensorRT-LLM for production inference.
learning_objectives: Train neural networks across multiple servers with PyTorch, Megatron-LM, and DeepSpeed
Use activation checkpointing, gradient accumulation, tensor, and pipeline parallelism to fit large models
Capture training performance characteristics to tune architectures and throughput
Deploy very large multi-GPU models using TensorRT-LLM and NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
courses.target_audience: Engineers deploying very large models to production
courses.technical_requirements: Strong PyTorch knowledge plus experience with deep learning, data parallel training, and distributed systems
courses.notes: Agenda covers large-model training foundations, memory-saving techniques, DeepSpeed/MoE tuning, TensorRT-LLM optimizations, Triton deployment, and a final assessment deploying a GPT checkpoint.

courses.title: Introduction to Deploying Gen AI Using NVIDIA NIM Microservices
courses.description: NVIDIA NIM is a set of easy-to-use microservices designed for secure, reliable deployment of high performance AI model inferencing across the cloud, data center and workstations. It is designed to speed up AI deployment in enterprises, supporting various optimized community AI models. This Deep Learning Institute (DLI) course covers important concepts to help developers understand how NIM enables the building, deploying, and scaling of AI applications.
learning_objectives: Describe the key features of NIM microservices
Perform self-hosted deployment of NIM microservices
Use NIM microservices to build an AI chatbot with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Discover and explore innovative AI applications built with NIM microservices
courses.target_audience: Developers and ML engineers deploying AI models in enterprise environments
courses.technical_requirements: Familiarity with artificial intelligence. Tools: NVIDIA NIM Inference Microservices, Docker
courses.notes: NVIDIA's deployment platform introduction. Covers self-hosted deployment of NIM microservices, building RAG chatbots, and exploring innovative AI applications. Designed to speed up enterprise AI deployment with secure, reliable inferencing across cloud, data center, and workstations.

courses.title: Sizing LLM Inference Systems
courses.description: Practical guide to sizing and optimizing LLM inference stacks using NVIDIA Inference Microservices (NIM). Learners analyze streaming/prefill/decoding flows, throughput versus latency trade-offs, tensor parallelism, in-flight batching, and KV caching, then benchmark models with GenAI-Perf to plan on-prem or cloud capacity that meets real-world workloads.
learning_objectives: Optimize and deploy models with NIM across streaming, prefill, and decoding modes
Analyze throughput/latency trade-offs and the impact of input/output lengths and batch sizes
Understand tensor parallelism, in-flight batching, chunked prefill, and KV caching for efficient scaling
Benchmark LLMs using GenAI-Perf and select inference hyperparameters that fit specific use cases
Perform cost-benefit analyses for on-prem versus cloud deployments to ensure sufficient capacity
courses.target_audience: AI practitioners responsible for planning or operating LLM inference infrastructure
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with Python programming, fundamentals of AI/ML, familiarity with LLM concepts
courses.notes: Covers NIM microservices, throughput vs. latency analysis, tensor parallelism, input/output length effects, chunked prefill, KV caching, GenAI-Perf benchmarking, inference hyperparameters, and on-prem vs. cloud cost/benefit strategies.

courses.title: Introduction to Deploying Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines for Production
courses.description: Hands-on lab that bridges proof-of-concept RAG apps to production-grade deployments. Learners size infrastructure, deploy Helm-based NVIDIA NIM stacks on Kubernetes, customize pipeline components, and stand up observability plus autoscaling so RAG systems handle enterprise traffic and document volume.
learning_objectives: Launch RAG pipeline applications onto Kubernetes using Helm and the NVIDIA NIM Operator
Leverage NVIDIA NIMs for scalable, containerized LLMs and embedding services
Connect, update, add, and autoscale pipeline components to meet demand
Monitor performance with Prometheus, Grafana, and DCGM
Plan infrastructure sizing steps that convert pilots into enterprise deployments
courses.target_audience: Engineers deploying RAG systems to production
courses.technical_requirements: Familiarity with LLM/RAG applications, Kubernetes, and Helm workflows
courses.notes: Covers infrastructure sizing, Helm-based deployments, NIM Operator, monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana/DCGM, and autoscaling via HPA and load tests.

courses.title: Deploying Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines for Production
courses.description: Instructor-led workshop for deploying enterprise-scale RAG and agentic pipelines with NVIDIA NIM microservices. Participants move from Docker Compose proofs of concept to Kubernetes clusters, deploy LLM/embedding/reranking NIMs via the NIM Operator, integrate PDF ingestion blueprints, monitor clusters with Prometheus/Grafana/DCGM, and autoscale workloads to handle multimodal traffic.
learning_objectives: Build simple RAG applications with API endpoints and Docker Compose
Deploy and manage NVIDIA NIM microservices (LLM, embeddings, rerankers) on Kubernetes using the NIM Operator
Integrate NIMs plus PDF ingestion workflows into production-grade pipelines
Monitor GPU and application health using Prometheus, Grafana, and DCGM
Implement Horizontal Pod Autoscaler with custom metrics and load tests to scale NIM services
Construct multimodal RAG pipelines that process text, figures, tables, and images end-to-end
courses.target_audience: Teams deploying enterprise RAG solutions
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with LLM/RAG applications, Kubernetes, Helm, and distributed deployments
courses.notes: Includes API prototypes, Docker Compose labs, NIM Operator deployments, PDF ingestion blueprints, Prometheus/Grafana monitoring, HPA scaling with Locust load tests, multimodal extraction (text/figures/tables/images), and a final assessment deploying an enterprise-grade RAG pipeline.

courses.title: Building Agentic AI Applications with Large Language Models
courses.description: The bar for what AI-powered agents can do has been steadily rising over the past few years, and new innovations allow them to not only engage in conversations but also utilize tools, conduct research, and execute on complex objectives at scale. This course empowers you to develop sophisticated agent systems that can execute on deep thought, research, software calling, and distributed operation. Throughout the course, you'll gain hands-on experience in designing agents that efficiently retrieve and refine information, intelligently route queries, and execute tasks concurrently using orchestration tools like LangGraph and sound software engineering practices. By the end of the course, you will have a solid foundation in agent architectures and will be able to construct interesting agent-like integrations to complement your existing workflows and software stacks.
learning_objectives: Understand the strengths and limitations of LLMs, and why agent-based paradigms help us to empower them in our modern software landscape
Learn to produce structured outputs to enable machine-parseable function calls or API integrations
Explore retrieval mechanisms and knowledge graphs for domain knowledge
Experiment with multi-agent orchestration using frameworks like LangGraph
courses.target_audience: Developers with introductory deep learning knowledge (including attention mechanisms and transformers), and intermediate Python proficiency (including object-oriented programming and familiarity with ML libraries). Experience from Getting Started with Deep Learning or Fundamentals of Deep Learning is preferred.
courses.technical_requirements: Introductory deep learning knowledge (including attention mechanisms and transformers). Experience from DLI's Getting Started with Deep Learning or Fundamentals of Deep Learning is preferred. Intermediate Python proficiency (including object-oriented programming and familiarity with ML libraries). Tutorials like Python Tutorial (w3schools.com) or equivalent practical experience suffice.
courses.notes: Workshop covers fundamentals of agent abstraction and LLMs, structured output and basic fulfillment mechanisms, retrieval mechanisms and environmental tooling, multi-agent systems and frameworks. Topics include LLM capabilities and pitfalls, agents as task decomposition abstraction, JSON/task-based outputs, domain alignment and schema enforcement, cognitive architectures, environment access strategies, tool interfaces for external data repositories, vector-RAG for semantic retrieval, task decomposition among specialized agents, communication buffers, process distribution schemes. Final assessment: deploy an agent that can schedule multiple retrieval operations to gather research and return to user. Optional section on real-time agents covering multimodal considerations, robotics, audio systems, and world models. Available in English.
